:::{#exm-entropy-uniform}
#### Entropy of a uniform random variable

Let $X$ be [uniformly distributed](random-variables.qmd#def-uniform) on the interval from $0$ to $a > 0$, as in @exm-surprisal-uniform.
By @thm-entropy-continuous,

$$
\ba
\entropyf{X}
&= -\int_0^a \tfrac{1}{a} \log \tfrac{1}{a} \, dx \\
&= \log a.
\ea
$$

Every value has the same [surprisal](#def-surprisal-continuous) $\log a$,
so its [expectation](#def-expectation) is also $\log a$.
With $a = \tfrac{1}{2}$ and logarithms to base 2, the [entropy](#def-entropy) is $-1$ bit.
The entropy of a [continuous random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-continuous-rv) can be negative [@cover2006elements, Example 8.1.1].
